stances.claim: The US Electoral College allows a presidential candidate to win the national popular vote yet lose the election -- a counter-democratic exception that happened in 2016 (Clinton-Trump) joining 1824, 1876, 1888, and 2000, demonstrable through a simplified 9-state worked example where 260,000 popular votes lose to 240,000 because of winner-takes-all elector allocation.

The Electoral College's per-elector population disparity -- Alaska's 750,000 inhabitants share 3 electors while California's 39 million share 55 -- gives every Alaskan almost thrice the voting power of every Californian, structurally violating one-person-one-vote at the presidential level even while it is observed at every other electoral level (senators, representatives, governors).

The Electoral College is a 'constitutional relic' -- a founding-father compromise between direct popular election and indirect congressional election -- that has been ridiculed even by Vladimir Putin ('And you call your presidential election democratic?'), and survives only because constitutional reform has retired biases against slaves and women but not the EC itself.
stances.rhetorical_move: relic-framing with comparative-reform argument (other biases removed, this one wasn't)

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban explains how Hillary Clinton won the 2016 US popular vote yet lost the presidency to Donald Trump -- and answers friends' how-and-why questions by walking through the Electoral College's quirks. American voters do not directly indicate presidential choices on their ballots; they vote for 'electors' who later vote for the prechosen candidate. Each of the 50 states plus DC allocates electors by local law, supposedly proportional to population -- California with 55, Alaska/Montana/Wyoming/DC with 3 each, totaling 538 with a 270-vote winning threshold under most states' winner-takes-all rule (except Maine and Nebraska). He demonstrates the anomaly with a simplified 9-state, 500,000-voter, 50-elector model: assuming Clinton gets 80% in State 1 (100,000 voters, 10 electors) and 45% in the 8 other states (50,000 each, 5 electors each), and Trump gets the inverse, Clinton totals 260,000 popular votes nationwide but earns only 10 electoral votes (State 1 alone), while Trump's 240,000 popular votes earn him 40 electoral votes from the other 8 -- and wins. He flags the per-elector population disparity (Alaska's 750,000 share 3 electors against California's 39M sharing 55), giving every Alaskan almost thrice the voting power of every Californian, and notes that this same Constitution has been reformed to remove biases against slaves and women but not against this 'constitutional relic' that even Vladimir Putin has mocked: 'And you call your presidential election democratic?'
